strings.name: Bill Winters
strings.role: Group Chief Executive of Standard Chartered
strings.summary: Bill Winters is an American banker who has led Standard Chartered as group chief executive since 2015, with business spanning cross-border finance in Asia, Africa and the Middle East. He previously co-led JPMorgan's investment bank, founded asset manager Renshaw Bay and contributed to UK banking reform advice.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026; recent activity is supported by the October 28 earnings-call transcript. Group and divisional roles, appointments and announcements are distinguished. Medium- and long-term targets are not treated as achieved results.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Standard Chartered and participates in cross-border financial services across Asian, African and Middle Eastern markets.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: He holds a bachelor's degree in international relations from Colgate University and an MBA from the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School.
strings.facts.f2.label: Identity and work location
strings.facts.f2.value: The UK company register records September 1961 as his birth month and American nationality. Standard Chartered's biography places his work base in London.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Banking reform advice
strings.highlights.h1.text: As an Independent Commission on Banking member, he contributed to financial stability and competition recommendations. These were collective work, not legislation written by him alone.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Climate finance involvement
strings.highlights.h2.text: He chaired the Taskforce for Scaling Voluntary Carbon Markets and participates in the Integrity Council's advisory work. Organizational involvement does not establish verified emissions reductions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Joins third-quarter results Q&A
strings.timeline.t1.text: Dialling in from Dubai, he discusses business and costs with the finance chief. Future return targets in the transcript remain forecasts.
strings.timeline.t2.title: CNA interview in Singapore
strings.timeline.t2.text: During the Milken Asia Summit, he discusses AI regulation, cybersecurity and human judgment. These views are attributed to him.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes UK chair of India-UK Financial Partnership
strings.timeline.t3.text: He works on closer links between the countries' financial services industries; this is not a government ministerial appointment.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes Standard Chartered group chief executive
strings.timeline.t4.text: After joining the group in May, he enters the board as group chief executive on June 10, succeeding Peter Sands.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Awarded a CBE
strings.timeline.t5.text: He is appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire for services to the UK economy and financial services. A CBE is not a knighthood.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Founds Renshaw Bay
strings.timeline.t6.text: He serves as the asset manager's chairman and CEO until joining Standard Chartered's board in 2015.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Independent Commission on Banking
strings.timeline.t7.text: He becomes a member of the UK government-established commission, chaired by John Vickers, which makes recommendations in 2011.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes co-CEO of JPMorgan's investment bank
strings.timeline.t8.text: He holds the role until 2009. It is joint leadership of the investment banking business, not the CEO role of the JPMorgan group.
